In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TP53 genetic screening should be offered to women with breast cancer onset before the age of thirty and to women with breast cancers with other features that are suggestive of LFS.

a young woman with a family history suggestive for LFS or a history of multiple LSF-related cancers, and a woman with breast cancer diagnosed at the age of 30 years or younger, should be tested for a TP53 mutation, irrespective of BRCA1/2 status and/or tumour characteristics.

TP53 germlinescreening is recommended for women diagnosed with breast and other LFS-related cancers before the age of thirty, and for women diagnosed with early onset breast cancer with additional LFS-related cancer, or a suggestive family history.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TP53 genetic screening should be considered in young women with breast cancer who have a family history suggestive for LFS or a previous diagnosis of LFS-related cancer, irrespective of the age of onset of breast cancer.
TP53 germlines testing is not indicated for women with breast cancers onset at age 31 years and older.
TP53 mutation testing should be considered in all young breast cancer women, irrespective of family history or personal cancer history.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TP53 germlin testing in women with early-onset breast cancers is not a routine practice, but that it is performed in a significant number of young breast cancer patients in the Netherlands.

the prevalence of TP53 mutations in early-onset (younger than 30 year of age) breast cancer is very low, and therefore, a very early age at diagnosis is not sufficient to warrant TP53 genetic testing in the absence of other LFS-associated features.
TP53 germlines testing in young women should only be performed when there is a strong clinical indication, such as a family history suggestive for LFS or multiple LFS-related cancers.
